name: Gerasene Demon
prompt:
A card picture for a 1990s-style fantasy trading card game, hand-made traditional media with visible texture, the matte, slightly faded look of a printed 1990s card. One clear subject that fills the frame, its focal point near the centre, readable at a glance even very small. Keep the bottom-left and bottom-right corners dark and simple. Landscape 3:2. No text, no letters, no inscriptions, no border, no frame, no logo, no watermark, no signature. Not photorealistic, not 3D render, not modern digital concept art, not anime, not a glossy oil painting.

Setting: the War in Heaven from the Bible (Genesis, 1 Enoch, Isaiah, Revelation): fallen angels, giants, demons and the beasts of the Apocalypse, shown as Christian sacred art showed them.

Look: a Romanesque church wall painting (fresco), 11th-12th century, the kind in Catalan and French apse paintings. Thick dark outlines, flat bands of earth and mineral colour: red ochre, yellow ochre, lapis blue, bone white and black; simple almond-eyed faces, stiff powerful poses, patterned borders of colour bands behind the figure. Cracked, flaking plaster with chalky, faded paint and patches of loss. Grotesque and unsettling like the demons of medieval wall paintings: distorted bodies, fangs, staring eyes, animal parts mixed with human ones, painted with stiff, naive conviction.

Subject: A demon of the Legion that possessed the man of the Gerasenes (Mark 5): a hunched, ash-grey fiend with bat ears, claws and a leering fanged mouth, breaking the iron chains on its wrists among the hillside tombs.
